lesson: In cache_key in keys.py, drop only gclid, fbclid, msclkid, and utm_ parameters except utm_content, rejecting blanket tracking-param heuristics or dropping all utm_ params.
why: utm_content routes A/B feature variants, so dropping it would cause the CDN to serve the wrong variant to experiment cohorts.
quote: utm_content stays in the key: that's a standing agreement with marketing-eng, because utm_content routes which A/B feature experience the page renders.

lesson: In keys.py, record dropped parameters using a counter tagged by parameter name instead of per-request log lines.
why: Edge request volume is too high and per-request logging would overwhelm the log collector.
quote: at edge volumes per-request logging would drown the collector; a counter tagged by param name is plenty, and only for the dropped ones.

lesson: In cache_key in keys.py, apply a stable sort by parameter name only, rejecting the proposal to sort values for repeated parameter names.
why: Origin endpoints sometimes treat the order of repeated parameter values as semantically meaningful requests.
quote: Some origin endpoints treat repeated-param order as meaningful, so tag=b&tag=a and tag=a&tag=b are legitimately different requests.

lesson: In cache_key in keys.py, completely drop any parameter with an empty value, overriding the retention exception even for utm_content.
why: Empty-valued parameters are ignored by origin handlers and merely fragment the cache.
quote: Drop them entirely - an empty-valued param never reaches the origin's handler logic, it just fragments the cache.

lesson: In cache_key in keys.py, lowercase only the scheme and host while preserving the path's case and trailing slashes, rejecting full URL lowercasing and slash stripping.
why: The origin object storage is case-sensitive, and stripping trailing slashes previously caused directory index endpoints to collide with file endpoints.
quote: Path case preserved, trailing slash preserved, exactly as given.

lesson: In cache_key in keys.py, omit the trailing '?' character when all query parameters are dropped.
why: URLs with only tracking parameters must map to the same cache key as URLs with no query string to preserve cache hit rates.
quote: if nothing survives the filter, the key is just scheme://host plus the path, no dangling question mark.
